newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish stocks close flat after directionless day.
newsitem.headline: Swedish stocks close flat after directionless day.

text.p: The Swedish bourse ended flat on Thursday after a lacklustre day, recovering lost ground in afternoon trade after Wall Street opened.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.02 percent to 2,125.90 after shares worth 3.2 billion crowns were traded.
Brokers said the market remained strong, even though it has backed off its all time high reached on Tuesday, but there was some uncertainty over the short-term direction.
"It's difficult to find a case to trade on," a broker said.
The strongest performer of the day was clothing retailer Hennes & Mauritz which jumped 28 crowns to 894 crowns.
The rise followed an unexpectedly strong quarterly and a report in Swedish business daily Dagens Industri saying Merrill Lynch had lifted its price expectation to 940-950 crowns.
Market heavyweights were higher. Telecoms Ericsson edged up 0.5 crown to 174 crowns and Astra was 2.5 higher at 297 crowns.
The banking and forestry sectors were the losers of the day, slipping 0.84 percent and 0.65 percent respectively.
Electrical engineering group ABB rose four to 723 crowns. The company named Goran Lindahl as the successor to Percy Barnevik who is to stay on as chairman from January 1 next year.
